entries.title: Ezekiel 34:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The shepherds - The rulers of the people kings, magistrates, and princes; as also priests, and prophets. Of Israel - The two tribes, and the few out of the ten that adhere to the house of David. That feed - Contrive their own ease, advantage, and honour.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ye kill - You contrive methods, to take first the life, and next the estate of the well - fed, the rich and wealthy. But - You take care to lead, protect, provide for, and watch over them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The diseased - The weak and languishing. Bound up - Oppressors in the state, or church, broke many then, but these shepherds bound them not up.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No shepherd - No vigilant, faithful shepherd. Became meat - Were made a prey of, and devoured by all their neighbours.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In the cloudy and dark day - In the time of general distress.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The fat - The powerful and rich. I will feed - I will judge and punish them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I judge - Between men and men, between the smaller and weaker, and the greater and stronger, as their different state requires I will do. The rams - Rulers, who also shalt be dealt with according to their behaviour.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But ye must tread down - You great ones, eat the fat, and sweet; and what you cannot eat, you waste and spoil. The deep waters - Which are sufficient for all.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will judge - I will vindicate the poor. The fat cattle - The rich. The lean - The poor.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: One shepherd - Christ, the great good, chief, only shepherd, that laid down his life for his sheep. My servant David - The seed of David, the beloved one, who was typified by David, and is in other places called by his name, as Jer 30:9 Eze 37:24 Isa 37:35 Hos 3:5. He shall feed - Do all the office of a good and faithful shepherd, and that for ever.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My servant - Christ was in this great work his fathers servant, Isa 42:1.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A covenant - A covenant of promises, which contain, and shall bring peace, that is all good.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Them - My returned captives, The places - All the country. My hill - Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A plant - The Messiah. The shame - The reproach.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Their God - By covenant, from their forefathers. Am with them - Present with them, and reconciled to them.
